summary: Benin is visa-free for citizens of every African country and free to enter for ECOWAS nationals, while all other visitors apply online for the official e-Visa (evisa.bj) before travel — there is no visa on arrival, and a yellow fever certificate is required from everyone.

payments.text: Cash rules — cards are accepted only at larger hotels and supermarkets in Cotonou, while mobile money (MTN MoMo, Moov) is used everywhere. Reliable ATMs are mostly limited to Cotonou and larger towns.

safety.text: Southern Benin, including Cotonou, is generally calm apart from petty crime, but the northern border areas — including Pendjari and W national parks — carry a serious risk of terrorist attack and kidnapping. Check advisories and avoid the far north.

source.name: U.S. Department of State — Benin Travel Advisory

bestTimeToVisit.text: November to February is the main dry season — harmattan air, cooler nights and the best conditions for the coast, Ouidah and Abomey; the south sees heavy rain from April to July.

tips.text: Avoid the areas bordering Burkina Faso and Niger, including Pendjari and W national parks — jihadist groups have attacked and kidnapped in the far north.
Apply for the e-visa only on the official portal (evisa.bj) — third-party sites charge steep mark-ups for the same document.
Your yellow fever certificate is checked before immigration at Cotonou airport — travellers without one can be refused entry or vaccinated on the spot at their own cost.
Carry CFA franc cash outside Cotonou and consider setting up mobile money — card acceptance is rare and ATMs are scarce up-country.
Zémidjan motorcycle taxis (yellow shirts) are the main way around Cotonou — agree the fare before setting off and ask for a helmet.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Benin?
faq.answer: Citizens of all African countries enter visa-free, and ECOWAS nationals enjoy full free movement. Everyone else — including EU, UK and US passport holders — must apply online for the official e-Visa at evisa.bj before travel; there is no visa on arrival.

faq.question: How much does the Benin e-visa cost?
faq.answer: Roughly EUR 50 for a 30-day single-entry visa, EUR 75 for 30-day multiple entry and EUR 100 for a 90-day multiple-entry visa. The exact amount is shown during the application, and approval normally takes a few business days.

faq.question: Is the yellow fever vaccine mandatory for Benin?
faq.answer: Yes — a yellow fever certificate is required from all travellers aged 9 months and over, whatever country you arrive from, and it is checked on arrival.

faq.question: Can I get a visa on arrival in Benin?
faq.answer: No. Benin replaced its visa-on-arrival scheme with the e-Visa — non-African visitors must hold an approved e-visa before boarding their flight.

faq.question: Is Benin safe to visit?
faq.answer: The south — Cotonou, Ouidah, Porto-Novo, Abomey and the coast — is generally calm apart from petty crime. The far north along the Burkina Faso and Niger borders, including the national parks, is high-risk and best avoided; check current advisories before travelling.
